facts.fact: The National Bank of Ethiopia revised its Licensing and Authorization of Payment Instrument Issuer Directive, raising the capital for a Payment Instrument Issuer company to 100 million Birr, per Ethiopian Monitor.
facts.system: Licensing and Authorization of Payment Instrument Issuer Directive

facts.fact: Ethiopian Monitor reports that the National Bank of Ethiopia made interoperability among mobile wallets mandatory and mandated financial institutions to participate in the Ethiopian Instant Payment System (EIPS).

The National Bank of Ethiopia on 12 May 2025 replaced its directive on Payment Instrument Issuers, the licensed non-bank e-money issuers, and raised their minimum paid-up capital from 50 million to 100 million birr.

The National Bank of Ethiopia issued Directive ONPS/10/2025, in force 12 May 2025, amending its directive on licensing and authorization of payment instrument issuers, setting capital, ownership and conduct requirements for licensed issuers.
